objections.claim_attacked: post-CTS optimization looked clean (placement utilization 71.5%, global-route overflow 3.8%)
objections.objection: 3.8% overflow concentrated in macro channels is not clean at 28nm. Clean pre-route is typically <0.5-1.0% overflow with no hotspots >2%. Team should have flagged at post-CTS global route, not first detailed route.
objections.corrected_version: Post-CTS showed 3.8% overflow with hotspots in six west channels; placement timing looked clean but congestion map already red. Reviewer would have stopped before detailed route.

objections.claim_attacked: 100 hard macros for ~1M placeable instances at 71.5% utilization
objections.objection: Ratio 1 macro per 10k cells is very macro-dense for DSP at 28nm. With 100 macros, effective placeable area is fragmented; 71.5% utilization excluding macros would leave almost no whitespace between macros, making 2-4 gcell channels inevitable and density screen 65% ineffective unless whitespace reclaimed elsewhere.
objections.corrected_version: Either ~40-60 macros for 1M instances, or 1M instances plus 100 macros implies effective utilization in macro-shadow is >85% locally; should report both macro-area ratio and std-cell-only utilization.

objections.claim_attacked: pin-swap on two macro instances to move high-fanout pins away
objections.objection: Hard macro pins (SRAM) are fixed in LEF; you cannot pin-swap like std-cell. Swapping two identical macro instances does not move pin locations unless you change orientation or logical-to-physical mapping. Term pin-swap mischaracterizes mechanism.
objections.corrected_version: Swap logical assignment of two macro instances (or flip orientation N vs FN) to move high-fanout logical pins away from most congested channel; requires checking that orientation is still legal and does not create new DRC.

objections.claim_attacked: global-route overflow dropped from 3.8% to 0.6% via density screen 65% + relaxed NDR on two mid-layers only
objections.objection: Magnitude of reduction 84% from only local density reduction ~6-10% in six narrow channels is optimistic. Density screen helps but does not create routing tracks. Relaxing NDR helps if NDR was cause, but for macro channel congestion the blocker is usually PG straps and pin access, not NDR. Would expect 3.8% -> ~1.5-2.0%, not 0.6%, without widening channels or thinning PG.
objections.corrected_version: Overflow 3.8% -> ~1.8% after screens + NDR relax, then to 0.6% after also thinning PG straps in channels or adding routing layer promotion and placement halo, requiring two incremental global route passes.

objections.claim_attacked: 214,000 DRC violations -> 340 on next route pass, then 0 after two repair iterations
objections.objection: Drop from 214k to 340 in one detailed route pass is too steep. Even if overflow was root cause, router would need to resolve opens/shorts iteratively. 214k concentrated DRCs typically decay to 20k-40k then 2k-5k then hundreds, not 99.8% in one pass. 340 after one pass suggests initial 214k number inflated or included phantom violations.
objections.corrected_version: 214k -> ~18k after first fix pass, -> ~1200 after second, -> 340 after third, -> 0 after two repair loops. Report should include intermediate counts.

objections.claim_attacked: unchanged utilization 71.5% with small WNS degradation -12 ps
objections.objection: -12 ps cost for density screen 65% in six channels plus cell spreading is optimistic at 28nm. Moving cells out of channels adds 5-15um detour on critical paths; typical cost is -30 to -60 ps WNS and may improve hold. -12 ps is plausible only if critical paths not in affected channels.
objections.corrected_version: WNS -25 to -50 ps after screen, recovered to -12 ps after incremental timing opt with useful skew; utilization unchanged globally because cells pushed to east side raising local density there.

missing_from_story: PG mesh and power stripe blockage in those six west channels - at 28nm with 100 macros, M4-M6 straps often consume 30-40% of tracks in channels and must be thinned
Clock tree impact - adding density screens in CTS-affected region changes insertion delay and skew; no mention of clock rerun or hold impact
Pin-access checker results for macros - whether DRCs were true short/spacing or M1-M2 pin access at macro boundary, which determines if NDR relax actually helps
Detailed route layer distribution of DRCs - which layers contributed to 214k and whether relaxed mid-layers were indeed the bottleneck vs M2/M3 pin layer
most_defensible_part: Rejecting floorplan channel widening because top-level feedthroughs and PG stripe locations were already derived and frozen - this is exactly the schedule-risk reason a veteran team would accept a local fix with small WNS cost rather than reopening top-level.
overall_note: Scenario is a real congestion failure mode at 28nm with macro-dense blocks, but numbers are over-idealized for a single-pass fix. With corrections to overflow baseline, gradual DRC decay, and proper description of macro remapping vs pin-swap, the episode becomes a strong teaching case for local density screens and targeted NDR relax as alternative to floorplan rework.
